answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network imposes superlinear stake burning per identity: creating the n-th agent demands destroying stake scaled by O(n^2). Even if an adversary anchors trust to an ancient verification relic, plants identities like resilient juniper shrubs across nodes, or operates from a barren server tundra, forging multiple puppet agents incurs exponential cost scaling, rendering mass entity replication economically ruinous.
